1:1:0: which is a first, indivisible instant with no time before it.
1:1:1: He made what did not exist into something that exists,
and in this no time at all is involved.
1:1:2: and therefore, of the demons, who die like human beings, as our Rabbis of blessed memory testified, it says "to demons, not to Eloah" (Devarim 32:17),
and of God, may He be blessed, it says "Eloah," for He is the absolutely eternal,
as it says "and he forsook the Eloah who made him."
And it says of Him "Elokim," in the plural,
to teach that He is the Form of all the eternal forms and of everything else,
as it says "the whole earth is full of His glory" (Yeshayahu 6:3),
for nothing apart from Him has any existence except what is emanated from His existence.
And no existing thing is found apart from His existence,
as it says "and You give life to them all" (Nechemiah 9:6).
And by way of likeness, every being separate from matter is called "Elokim,"
and the expert judges are called "Elokim" when they judge in the image of Elokim.
And to show the loftiness of His eternity, from which the eternity of the other separate beings is emanated,
it is said that He is the God of gods.
1:1:3: The word "sham" (there) denotes a distant place,
and every plural ending with a patach before it, stressed on the next-to-last syllable, denotes two equal things.
So the word "shamayim" denotes a body that is distant in relation to us by two equal distances on every side.
And this can only happen in a sphere that revolves in perfect roundness.
So it is saying that He created that body which is now distant from us on every side by two equal distances, and that is the sphere.
And that is why it did not say "created heavens," for it is not called so in itself but only in relation to our place.
1:1:4: the center fit for the sphere.
1:2:0: And the earth was tohu and bohu.
And that earth, which was created then, was a thing compounded of a first matter called tohu,
and of a first form called bohu.
For indeed the first matter was fit for only one form,
which was necessarily the first of all the forms of compounded things.
And by this it is made clear that the first matter is a newly created thing.
And the matter of that first compound is called tohu,
because in itself it is only something potential, not existing in actuality,
as it says "for they are tohu" (Shmuel I 12:21),
meaning they do not exist in actuality but only in the imagination.
And the form borne by that first compound is called bohu,
for "bo hu" — in it, in the tohu just mentioned, it exists in actuality.
And it calls "stones of bohu" (Yeshayahu 34:11) a subject that does not keep its form for any significant time,
as happened to the subject of the first form, which at once put on the different forms of the elements.
1:2:1: That is the dark air emanated then from the first compound, which was on the face of the deep,
on the face of the two lower elements, which were also emanated then from the first compound and surrounded one another:
1:2:2: The movers of the sphere, which are called "spirit,"
as it says "He makes the winds His messengers" (Tehillim 104:4).
1:2:3: Hovering over the face of the waters.
They then moved the dark air over the face of the waters that then surrounded the element of earth.
And so it came about that the part of it next to the sphere was set aflame by its motion,
and the part of it close to the water then took on some coldness from the water,
except for a small part of it that is warmed by chance through the turning of sparks from the luminaries of light.
1:3:0: That is the light of the seven days, which was for the needs of things that came into being without seed,

and it will be there in the future, as our Rabbis of blessed memory said (last chapter of Ketubot), that it will then serve what the land is destined to bring forth — cakes and fine woolen garments — not by the power of seed.
1:4:0: And Elokim saw the light, that it was good.
for Elokim saw and chose its existence because of its purpose, which is the good for whose sake He brought it into being through His active knowledge:
1:4:1: And Elokim separated between the light and the darkness.
Those days in which the first light served
had times of light and times of darkness,
not through the revolution of a sphere,
but through the divine will, which separated between the time of light and the time of darkness.
1:5:0: And Elokim called the light day.
Even though the time of light and darkness was not then conducted in the way that the time we now call by the names day and night is conducted for us:
1:5:1: And there was evening and there was morning.
Even though He separated the light and the darkness so that they would serve at different, separate times without the revolution of a sphere,
He separated them gradually, so that between them there was a time of evening as night came and a time of morning as day came:
1:6:0: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters.
Let there be a nature in the midst of the elemental waters,
like a sphere within them all around, separating some of them from others in form,
so that some upper part of the waters, toward the air, would turn to a vaporous nature.
And so they necessarily rose to some boundary in the elemental air,
and the air necessarily underwent some compression, to make room for the part that turned to vapor and spread out into a place far larger than its first place.
1:7:0: And since, when some of the elemental waters went away from beneath that part of them which had turned to a vaporous nature,
as happened when it said "let the waters be gathered from under the heavens,"
the vaporous part should then have come down into that place from which those waters had gone,
He made that separating firmament have in it a restraining force that holds back the vaporous part so that it does not come down,
and that is "the waters that are above the firmament,"
so that the compressed airy part came down and the vapor remained in its first place.
And therefore, when the moist vapor reaches there it thickens and produces rain, snow and hail,
and as they thicken they grow heavy and come down,
as it says "at the sound of His giving, there is a roar of waters in the heavens."
By saying "the heavens" he means the firmament that compresses the airy part,
as it says "and Elokim called the firmament heavens,"
and when the hot, smoky vapor reaches there it produces thunder and lightning,
as it says "He raises clouds from the end of the earth, He makes lightning for the rain."
And the fact that some of the heavy element of water is above the light air that is near us, against their nature,
shows without doubt the action of a willing Agent who intends a purpose,
as it says "and the firmament tells of the work of His hands."
1:7:1: It remained standing so, against its nature.
1:8:0: And Elokim called the firmament heavens.
Because the actions of the heavenly bodies reach us by means of it,
as it says "And Elokim set them in the firmament of the heavens to give light on the earth, and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate," and so on.
1:9:0: Not that they should dry up,
as many thought, saying that the drying of the exposed part of the earth happened through the power of the heavenly configurations.
Rather, He commanded that they be gathered to one place and not pass beyond it,
and so they are higher than the land and do not fall upon it, as the senses testify,
as it says "You set a boundary they may not pass, so that they do not return to cover the earth" (Tehillim 104:9).
1:10:0: And Elokim called the dry land earth.
He called the part by the name of the whole,
for indeed this part was the main intent of all of them,
as it says (Yeshayahu 45:18) "He formed it to be inhabited."
1:10:1: And Elokim saw that it was good.
He willed it so for the sake of the purpose, which is the intended good.
1:11:0: Kinds of plants for animals to eat,
as it says (Yoel 2:22) "for the pastures of the wilderness have sprouted grass."
1:11:2: Fruit trees making fruit after their kind.
For a cross of two kinds will not reproduce.
1:11:3: It was established so, without allowing more or less,
so that if a plant crossed from two kinds should occur, it will not reproduce.
1:14:0: Let there be luminaries in the firmament of the heavens.
In that firmament that was formed on the second day,
let there be the spark of the luminaries,
and there let it grow strong and be tempered to bring about in the lower world everything said in the passage,
just as the senses show that the light of a spark grows stronger as it passes through clear water.
1:15:0: To give light on the earth.
That light should come to it from the luminaries, tempered to suit its inhabitants.
1:15:1: That tempering, which was made necessary by His command, was established so:
1:16:0: And He made… and He set… to give light… and to rule… and to separate… that it was good.
Of the luminaries and the other stars it said "and He made,"
for they were included among the parts of the spheres, or the heavens,
whose creation it had already told (Bereshit 1:1),
and so it did not mention creation for them, only making.
And that is, that He brought them forth from some of the parts of the spheres, in a spherical shape and a shining form.
1:16:1: That is, that He intended by this the good,
which is the fitting purpose of His act.
1:18:0: And to rule over the day and over the night.
To bring new things into being in the lower world,
and they were needed then, together with the one light, for the coming into being of living creatures, which are more honored than the plants:
1:18:1: To separate between the light and the darkness.
To separate in the lower world, by their rising and setting, between the time of light, which He called day, and the time of darkness, which He called night,
as it said above, "to separate between the day and the night."
1:20:0: Let birds fly above the earth across the face of the firmament of the heavens.
To clear the air of the earth for its inhabitants of some excess moisture sent down from the firmament formed on the second day, by means of the spark acting in it.
1:21:0: And Elokim created the great sea creatures.
For the generative power set in the waters was not enough to bring forth the first sea creatures without seed,
until He created then a power sufficient for this.
1:22:0: For the purpose would not be reached in them except when they were many.
1:24:0: Let the earth bring forth living creatures.
The animal soul, added to the vegetative:
1:24:1: so that if a cross of two kinds should newly arise, it will not reproduce:
1:25:0: And Elokim made the beasts of the earth after their kind.
He gave each kind the special properties and senses that kind needs.
1:26:0: He then gave power to His heavenly household to bestow the image upon the subject prepared for it.
1:26:1: One kind among the kinds of living creatures that I have formed, whose name is man,
as it says "and man became a living creature" (Bereshit 2:7) — let us make him:
1:26:2: For it is an intellectual and eternal being,
and with this God, may He be blessed, opened a door in His Torah to acquiring knowledge of the separate beings through knowledge of our own soul.
1:26:3: In the matter of deeds, in which he will somewhat resemble the heavenly household,
in that they act with knowledge and awareness.
Yet their action is not by choice,
and in this man does not resemble them.
And in some way man resembles God, may He be blessed, who acts by choice.
Yet the choice of God, may He be blessed, is always for good,
which is not so with human choice.
And beyond this, the divine choice is in a far loftier manner than human choice.
That is why it says "kidmutenu" — like our likeness,
1:27:0: In the image of Elokim.
The word "Elokim," by way of likeness, is said of every being that is intellect in complete actuality, separate from matter,
and by this it is necessarily eternal.
That is why it is said of God, may He be blessed, and of His angels,
and likewise it is said of the judges, on account of the intellectual part fitting in them.
But since the human intellect, even though its act of understanding is without any material instrument,
and it reaches to what is not sensed and to some future things,
and it does not weaken by much use of its understanding, nor in the time of the body's old age,
but grows stronger,
and from all this it is clear without doubt that it is separate from matter,
for indeed the opposite of all these happens to the material powers of the body,
nevertheless, before it reflects, since it is then lacking every perfection that was prepared for it,
it is not called "Elokim" but only "the image of Elokim,"
until it acquires perfection, in particular in the wisdom through which it acquires love of God and fear of Him,
for then it will be an intellectual being in complete actuality, separate from matter,
and from this it follows that it will be eternal and lasting even after the death of the body.
And since it is within man's choice to acquire this perfection by striving to reflect on that wisdom,
it is made clear that when he holds himself back from this,
his intellectual power will remain as it was, lacking every perfection in actuality, as it was at first,
and it will go up into tohu and be lost,
as it says "man in his honor who does not understand is likened to the beasts; they are alike" (Tehillim 49:21),
and all this God, may He be blessed, taught in two words when He said "in the image of Elokim."
1:28:0: That you should protect your border with your intellect and keep the wild beasts from entering your boundaries,
and you will rule over them.
1:28:1: With traps and nets, to subdue them to your service:
1:30:0: And to every beast of the earth.
But to every beast of the earth, and to the animals and the birds, I have given all green herbs for food,
the kinds of herbs that do not yield seed.
1:31:0: Everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good.
The purpose of existence as a whole is very good, more than the particular purposes that are directed toward it.
1:31:1: The first one, which was the beginning of every sixth day,
on which all the work is finished so as to rest on Shabbat,
as it says (Shemot 20:9-10) "and do all your work, and the seventh day is Shabbat."
2:1:0: By reaching the purpose of existence as a whole:
2:2:0: And Elokim finished on the seventh day.
At the start of the seventh day,
which is the indivisible instant that is the beginning of the time to come and not a part of it,
as our Rabbis of blessed memory said (Bereshit Rabbah 10:9): He entered it by a hair's breadth.
2:2:1: And He rested on the seventh day.
That whole day was set apart from the first six days in the matter of rest.
2:3:0: And Elokim blessed the seventh day.
He blessed every seventh day to come,
that it should be more prepared than the other days, with an extra soul, "to shine with the light of life" (Iyov 33:30),
as our Rabbis said: once he has rested, "woe, the extra soul is lost" (Beitzah 16a).
